decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “Search”; Round 1 client (line 82): “I can see it … searching … That part feels good.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. Search is presented and approved, but the transcript does not establish whether it covers title, description, note, and URL as required, so divergence cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “sorting”; Round 1 client (line 82): “I can see it … sorting them … That part feels good.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. The recorded sorting behavior conforms to list sorting; the reference does not mandate a particular sort key.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “list/grid views”; Round 1 client (line 82): “it looks really nice” and mentions seeing a generic description and a “New” tag.
decisions.note: Prototype review. A list view and some item content are evidenced, but the transcript does not establish whether every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon, so divergence is indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “Add … bookmark flows”; Round 1 client (line 82): “I can see it saving links” and “When I paste a web address.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. Saving a bookmark through URL entry conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11): “delete bookmark flows”; Round 1 client (line 82): “I can see it … deleting” and “The only choice on a saved item is Delete.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. Bookmark deletion is recorded as working.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11) presents an add flow; Round 1 client (line 82): “Saving doesn't pull in the link's info,” “I have to type the title myself,” and asks it to fill the title and description from the link.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Manual title entry and a generic description diverge from automatic metadata collection; the client identifies the mismatch and supplies the expected automatic behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client (line 82) states the expectation that details come “from the link,” then explicitly accepts a departure: “a stand-in/simulated version is fine — it doesn't need to really go fetch from the internet.” Round 2 maker (line 145) presents simulated metadata discovery.
decisions.note: Specification gate leading into implementation review. Simulation is not equivalent to collecting metadata from the remote page, but the client explicitly identifies and accepts that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client (line 82), reacting to the presented add flow: “every new bookmark just gets … a ‘New’ tag” and “I need to be able to … adjust its tags.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. Fixed automatic tagging without user adjustment diverges from user tag assignment; the client requests adjustable tags.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (line 11) presents add and delete flows; Round 1 client (line 82): “I can't edit a bookmark after saving. The only choice … is Delete,” then requests changing title, description, collection, and tags.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Post-save editing is absent. The client requests the missing editing capability, including correction of title and description after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (line 145): metadata discovery “fills the title, description, and suggested tags automatically”; Round 2 client (line 223) repeats those fields and says they are “exactly what I needed,” without mentioning favicon or preview image.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The enumerated metadata omits the required favicon and preview image. The client's approval does not explicitly identify or accept those omissions.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (line 145) presents automatic title/description filling plus an Edit action; Round 2 client (line 223): “I can still tweak them” and confirms title and description can be changed through Edit.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The auto-filled title and description remain editable, including after saving, which conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (line 145): Edit changes “URL, title, description, collection, and tags”; Round 2 client (line 223) repeats that list and approves it, but neither presentation nor response includes editing the bookmark note.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The revised edit scope still omits the required note field. The client does not surface that difference, so final approval is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (line 145) says tags can be changed in Edit; Round 2 client (line 223) confirms automatic tags “can still” be tweaked and that Edit changes tags.
decisions.note: Implementation review. User-adjustable plural tags conform to assigning one or more tags.
